question: Does relational input access explain the classifier Fourier advantage?
run_name: Can the classifier read relations? | visible cube | raw vs particle vs relative
primary_endpoint: Selected held-out balanced BCE: particle-minus-raw, relative-minus-raw and relative-minus-particle. Simultaneous paired IID-context intervals; exact min validation BCE selects weights. k=1..4 output Fourier fixed in every arm. Frozen A/B/C/D mode-shape swaps include the same three representation contrasts, each on B-minus-A, C-minus-A and D-minus-A (nine simultaneous descriptive intervals). Common-rotation invariance diagnoses content separately.
decision_rule: All three fits must plateau after at least32k and no more than64k updates; otherwise unresolved. Material gain needs paired BCE upper95 < -0.002 and concordant increased AUC. Eligibility for RL additionally requires B-minus-A mode-content BCE contrast to raw upper95 < -0.002 and higher B AUC. That grid interval is descriptive, not IID population uncertainty. No automatic representation choice or RL launch. Summarize first; reviewer chooses particle or relative explicitly.
scope: Same archived scalar c, truth y and source y, lifted to two unit visible vectors with independent uniform common rotation. No truth function, parity or mode ID enters learned models. C explicitly encodes a structural relation; it is a diagnostic prior, not prior-free discovery. k1 particle harmonics duplicate Cartesian components; C repeats its8 extras to match B's16-slot amplitude, not active rank. No new seeds, changed truth, capacity search, policy updates, remote work or uploads. This is a separately reviewed follow-on to the completed18-round campaign; that ledger and paused automation remain untouched.
